name: Ortur H20 10W
tagline: Entry H20 chassis with integrated design and Ortur app workflow
tldr: Ortur H20 10W is the base diode tier on the H20 frame: faster traverse than LM3 with a more enclosed integration. Good for engraving and light cuts; step up to 20W or 40W for thicker wood.
mainObjective: High-quality hobby and light-business engraving with light, slow cutting

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

pros: Class 1 enclosure with lid lock, exhaust fan and emergency stop
Motorized lifting platform takes objects up to 98 mm tall
Fine ~0.08 × 0.09 mm spot for detailed engraving
cons: Slow cutting: ~14–24 min for a 3 mm basswood 10 × 10 cm square in our benchmarks
Manual focus on this module; Ortur only autofocuses the top module
High price for the laser power: most of the cost is the enclosure
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 10W SKU on Ortur H20. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other modules via the chips before buying.
proTips: Run material test grids at engraving speeds first. Add air assist for light cuts on basswood. If cut jobs exceed ~30% of your week, compare the 20W or 40W module profiles before upgrading.

moduleSystem.headline: Swappable diode & IR modules
moduleSystem.description: H20 ships as a chassis with swappable 10W, 20W, or 40W diode modules and optional 2W IR heads for metal marking: verify which module is in the box.

editorialDepth.advantages: The 10W diode module on Ortur H20 is right when you mostly engrave wood, leather, and slate and should not pay for cut watts you will not use weekly. Same chassis, upgrade path later.
editorialDepth.limitations: Skip this module if you cut 5 mm+ stock daily: open the 20W or 40W profile. Cast acrylic and bare metal without spray stay frustrating on diode.

faq.question: Why pay over $1,100 for a 10W enclosed machine?
faq.answer: You pay for the enclosure, not the cutting power: Ortur lists a Class 1 enclosure with a light-blocking viewing cover, exhaust fan, lid safety lock, emergency stop and a motorized lifting platform for objects up to 98 mm tall. Ortur's store listed the 10W at $1,109 in October 2026, but out of stock.

faq.question: What can the H20 10W cut?
faq.answer: In our benchmarks a 10 × 10 cm square in 3 mm basswood takes about 14–24 min at 2–3 mm/s. Basswood up to about 5 mm and thin leather are possible in passes. Ortur describes this module as suited to light cutting, without thickness figures.

faq.question: Start with the 10W and upgrade the module later?
faq.answer: The H20 takes interchangeable modules, so it is possible. Compare first: in October 2026 Ortur listed the 20W version at $1,379 with a free air pump and the 40W at $1,909. If you expect to cut weekly, the bundle gap may be cheaper than buying a second module later.

standoutFeatures.title: Class 1 enclosure
standoutFeatures.body: Lid safety lock, emergency stop, exhaust fan and a light-blocking viewing cover: usable in a shared room.

standoutFeatures.title: Motorized lifting platform
standoutFeatures.body: The bed lowers for objects up to 98 mm tall, handy for boxes and thick blanks.

standoutFeatures.title: Infrared combo available
standoutFeatures.body: Ortur sells a 10W + 2W IR version ($1,748 in October 2026) for marking metal and plastics.
